title: M3.1 Pedagogical Quality Engine implementation
purpose: Implement the accepted deterministic pedagogical-quality engine, Atlas authoring skill, Studio diagnostics and browser/Pages execution boundary without changing the canonical kit contract or learner runtime.
invariants: learnit.kit.v2 schema and existing canonical validators remain read-only upstream authorities.
The quality engine is deterministic, read-only, local, network-free and shared by CLI, CI and Studio.
JavaScript renders the Python report but does not duplicate pedagogical rules.
Canonical invalid input can never receive PASS_ATLAS_PEDAGOGICAL_PROFILE_V1.
M3.1 introduces no new profile blocker beyond canonical validity and does not silently revise export validity.
The exact two-claim Atlas topology remains first practice to first validation, then first validation to second validation; no third transfer claim is required.
No scalar 0-100 score is a release authority.
EXCELLENT_BY_PROFILE is a static authoring-profile statement only, not proof of learning effectiveness.
AI self-iteration must stop rather than invent source-unsupported content.
No learner runtime, backend, account, sync, document-ingestion product path, runtime AI, Gate3, Gate4 or M4+ capability is introduced.
The promoted learner artifact remains exactly 366412 bytes with the frozen SHA-256.
requiredEvidence: Exact implementation scope with no QA-path overlap.
Both canonical proof kits pass frozen validators unchanged.
Deterministic byte-identical quality report for identical input.
Each frozen warning/advice rule is independently exercised.
No M3.1 rule requires a third independence claim.
CLI exit behavior for canonical invalid, profile pass and require-excellent.
Quality engine performs no write or network operation.
Studio consumes the Python report and clearly separates canonical validity, pedagogical quality and export availability.
Pages copies and executes the exact pedagogical-quality Python source.
Local Studio and Pages produce equivalent reports for the same draft.
Atlas authoring skill targets current contract and exact CLI.
Learner regressions and exact artifact identity PASS.
Repository governance and PR scope PASS.
Independent QA binds the exact frozen product HEAD before any final PASS.
adversarialTests: Malformed or canonical-invalid kit must never receive a positive quality verdict.
Course duration inconsistency must be reported without changing the kit.
Duplicate same-objective stimuli must be detected even when canonical claims do not link the duplicate pair.
Transfer difficulty not greater than first practice must warn.
Unexpected two-claim topology or weak basis must warn without requesting a third claim.
Single interaction type, same validation type and absent alternate representation must remain advisory only.
CLI --require-excellent must fail on non-excellent canonical content without mutating it.
Browser JavaScript must contain no PQ_* rule implementation.
Pages authority bundle must byte-match the repository Python quality engine.
External network and learner storage boundaries must remain unchanged.
Any changed path outside the exact allowlist yields HOLD.
nonGoals: LLM calls inside Studio or learner runtime
independentReview: Parent design was challenged under Linus and Steve perspectives and accepted with a subsequent claim-topology correction.
Repository governance and PR scope gate the product PR.
QA-WP-021 uses disjoint QA-only paths and must bind one exact frozen product HEAD.
A short author-facing desktop human gate occurs only after product PASS, independent QA PASS and candidate Pages deployment.
rollback: Revert the M3.1 product paths to the M3.0 promoted authoring behavior. No learner data, schema or canonical kit migration is involved.
